messages.subject: Forward-Mode Auto Diff Problems
parts:
Hi,

I'm currently working on the forward-mode auto diff and I have 3 questions/problems:

1) I'm not sure how to approach binary_log_loss, binom_coeff_log, and lmgamma.

2) For fmin/fmax, I am getting an error that "fmax" is ambiguous when I have something like fmax(x1.val_, x2.val_). I think this is because there is no fmax method for double, double. I tried to add one to stan/agrad/special_functions, but I keep getting an error.

3) I've also run into a problem with Phi (described below).

In the fvar.hpp file I have
template <typename T>
inline
fvar<T>
phi(const fvar<T>& x) {
using std::exp;
using std::sqrt;
using stan::math::Phi;
return fvar<T>(Phi(x.val_), x.d_ * exp(-x.val_ * x.val_ / 2) /
sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()));
}

and in fvar_test.cpp file I have
TEST(AgradFvar, phi) {
using stan::agrad::fvar;
using std::exp;
using std::sqrt;
using stan::math::Phi;

fvar<double> x(0.5);
x.d_ = 1.0;

fvar<double> a = Phi(x);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(Phi(0.5), a.val_);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(exp(-0.5 * 0.5 / 2) /
sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()), a.d_);

fvar<double> b = Phi(-x);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(Phi(-0.5), b.val_);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(-exp(-0.5 * 0.5 / 2) /
sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()), b.d_);
}

but I keep getting the following errors:

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Forward-Mode Auto Diff Problems
parts:
Peter,

Write the binomial coefficient as a product of logs (or a sum of log gammas) and then use the digamma function (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamma_function). Same for lngamma. Boost provides a convenient implementation (http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_52_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/digamma.html).

-Mike

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Forward-Mode Auto Diff Problems
parts:
On 1/31/13 8:28 AM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> Peter,
>
> Write the binomial coefficient as a product of logs (or a sum of log gammas) and then use the digamma function (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamma_function). Same for lngamma. Boost provides a convenient implementation (http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_52_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/digamma.html).

In general, you can crib off what we did for agrad/agrad.hpp
and agrad/special_functions.hpp.

Some more below.

> On Jan 30, 2013, at 11:53 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>
>> Hi,
>>
>> I'm currently working on the forward-mode auto diff and I have 3 questions/problems:
>>
>> 1) I'm not sure how to approach binary_log_loss, binom_coeff_log, and lmgamma.

Just look at the definition of the functions (which you'll
find, if nowhere else, in the agrad/agrad.hpp and agrad/special_functions.hpp
doc for the functions) and then calculate the partials with respect to
the arguments.

I've been trying to add more mathematical definitions to the doc.
I just added log loss, because that's the least standard of the
above. I'd like to also add all their partials with respect to
their arguments to the doc.

The Wikipedia page on gamma gives you the derivative of
the gamma function in terms of the digamma function (also
available in Boost and used in stan/agrad/special_functions.hpp),
so you just use the chain rule to figure out the derivative
of log gamma.

You'll also find the definition of binary_log_loss in the
doc in the agrad files.

>> 2) For fmin/fmax, I am getting an error that "fmax" is ambiguous when I have something like fmax(x1.val_, x2.val_). I think this is because there is no fmax method for double, double. I tried to add one to stan/agrad/special_functions, but I keep getting an error.

Can you dump out more of the error message you're getting
for fmax(). The rule is that the arguments have to uniquely
specify a function implementation and there's a long chain
of rules to figure out which of those functions it is. If
the compiler's telling you it's ambiguous, then there are
two equally acceptable definitions.

You can use explicit naming to disambiguate, for instance
explicitly using the double-based implementation of fmax
boost::math::fmax(x1.val_,x2.val_).
>> 3) I've also run into a problem with Phi (described below).
This is the key error message:

>> lib/boost_1.52.0/boost/math/special_functions/erf.hpp:123:9: error: invalid
>> operands to binary expression ('stan::agrad::fvar<double>' and 'int')
>> if(z < 0)

You need to define the comparison operators for fvar
and templated alternative types.

- Bob

parts:
No kidding. Peter's been tearing up the implementation.
It looks like he'll be done with what I thought would be
a semester-plus long project before midterms. Which is
great, because we have all sorts of more interesting (but
not really more mission critical) things to do after this.

- Bob

On 1/31/13 4:56 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> This is great!
> On Jan 30, 2013, at 11:53 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>
>> Hi,
>>
>> I'm currently working on the forward-mode auto diff and I have 3 questions/problems:
>>
>> 1) I'm not sure how to approach binary_log_loss, binom_coeff_log, and lmgamma.
>>
>> 2) For fmin/fmax, I am getting an error that "fmax" is ambiguous when I have something like fmax(x1.val_, x2.val_). I think this is because there is no fmax method for double, double. I tried to add one to stan/agrad/special_functions, but I keep getting an error.
>>
>> 3) I've also run into a problem with Phi (described below).
>>
>> In the fvar.hpp file I have
>> template <typename T>
>> inline
>> fvar<T>
>> phi(const fvar<T>& x) {
>> using std::exp;

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Forward-Mode Auto Diff Problems
parts: Thanks for all of the feedback.

On Jan 31, 2013, at 3:07 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:

Can you dump out more of the error message you're getting
for fmax().  The rule is that the arguments have to uniquely
specify a function implementation and there's a long chain
of rules to figure out which of those functions it is.  If
the compiler's telling you it's ambiguous, then there are
two equally acceptable definitions.

You can use explicit naming to disambiguate, for instance
explicitly using the double-based implementation of fmax
boost::math::fmax(x1.val_,x2.val_).

I ended up using std::max and std::min from the algorithm library because I could not find the file where the boost::math::fmax function comes from.

Thanks,
Peter

parts: I have one more question about what I need to do to implement Phi and whether my lmgamma derivative implementation is correct (both below).
On Jan 31, 2013, at 3:07 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
This is the key error message:

>> lib/boost_1.52.0/boost/math/special_functions/erf.hpp:123:9: error: invalid
>>       operands to binary expression ('stan::agrad::fvar<double>' and 'int')
>>    if(z < 0)

You need to define the comparison operators for fvar
and templated alternative types.

I'm not exactly sure how to go about this. 

I tried this:

//comparison operators

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const fvar<T1>& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2) {
      return x1.val_ < x2.val_;
    }

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const fvar<T1>& x1, const T2& x2) {
      return x1.val_ < x2;
    }

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const T1& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2) {

On Jan 31, 2013, at 8:28 AM, Michael Betancourt wrote:

Peter,

Write the binomial coefficient as a product of logs (or a sum of log gammas) and then use the digamma function (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamma_function).  Same for lngamma.  Boost provides a convenient implementation (http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_52_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/digamma.html).  

-Mike

Thanks for the help. I did this for lmgamma, but it got a little messy with the product function depending on one of the inputs. Could someone please check my code (below)?

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline
    fvar<typename stan::return_type<T1,T2>::type>
    lmgammaa(const fvar<T1>& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2){
      using stan::math::lmgamma;
      using boost::math::tgamma;
      using std::log;
      double deriv = 0;
      int count;
      for(count = 1; count < x2.val_ - 1; count++)
deriv += (x1.d_  - x2.d_) / tgamma(x1.val_ - (x2.val_ - count) / 2);
      deriv += x1.d_ / tgamma(x1.val_);
      deriv += (2 * x2.val_ - 1) / 2 * log(boost::math::constants::pi<double>()) * x2.d_;
      return fvar<typename 
                  stan::return_type<T1,T2>::type>(lmgamma(x1.val_, x2.val_), deriv);
    }


Other than that, everything else (binary infix operators, unary prefix operators, absolute functions, bounds functions, arithmetic functions, rounding functions, power and logarithm functions, trig functions, hyperbolic trig functions, link functions, probability-related functions, combinatorial functions, and compose functions) is done and tested.



Thanks,
Peter

Hi Peter,

Can you double-check the binomial_coefficient_log implementations? You've got calls to gamma(), which I think should be tgamma(). That's causing our windows build to break. It can't find the right gamma() to call. I don't know where clang++ and g++ on Mac is finding gamma().

Once all the references are changed to tgamma(), we run into another problem of the result being too large to represent. I don't think you need tgamma() to calculate what you're doing since we're working on the log-scale. Let me know if you need help working through the derivatives.


Daniel

PS. If you're not on the build status distribution, you can see it here: https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!forum/stan-buildbot

Hi,

For lgamma, the derivative should be digamma / tgamma?

If this is the case, then we still run into a problem with the derivative being too large, since for 
N - n > 1000 or N > 1000, we have binomial_coefficient_log = n * log(N - n) + (N + 0.5) * log(N/(N-n))  + 1/(12*N) - n - 1/(12*(N-n)) - lgamma(n + 1.0).

So when we differentiate the lgamma(n + 1.0), we'd get 
n.d_ * digamma(n + 1.0) / tgamma(n + 1.0), which still results in an error for large n. I'm not too sure what to do about this term.

But for the derivative as a whole (in terms of x1.d_ and x2.d_) I got 
x2.d_ * log(x1.val_ - x2.val_) + (x2.val_ * (x1.d_ - x2.d_)) / (x1.val_ - x2.val_) + x1.d_ * log(x1.val_ / (x1.val_ - x2.val_)) + (x1.val_ + 0.5) / (x1.val_ / (x1.val_ - x2.val_)) * (x1.d_ * (x1.val_ - x2.val_) - (x1.d_ - x2.d_) * x1.val_) / ((x1.val_ - x2.val_) * (x1.val_ - x2.val_)) + x1.d_ / (12 * x1.val_ * x1.val_) - x2.d_ + (x1.d_ - x2.d_) / (12 * (x1.val_ - x2.val_) * (x1.val_ - x2.val_)) - digamma(x2.val_ + 1) * x2.d_ / tgamma(x2.val_ + 1).


Thanks,
Peter

On Feb 4, 2013, at 5:48 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:

Hi Peter,

Can you double-check the binomial_coefficient_log implementations? You've got calls to gamma(), which I think should be tgamma(). That's causing our windows build to break. It can't find the right gamma() to call. I don't know where clang++ and g++ on Mac is finding gamma().

Once all the references are changed to tgamma(), we run into another problem of the result being too large to represent. I don't think you need tgamma() to calculate what you're doing since we're working on the log-scale. Let me know if you need help working through the derivatives.


Daniel

PS. If you're not on the build status distribution, you can see it here: https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!forum/stan-buildbot

parts:
Nope, digamma is the derivative of lgamma (http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/digamma.html).

This means that the derivative of tgamma is actually digamma * tgamma.

On Feb 4, 2013, at 7:03 PM, Peter Li wrote:

> Hi,
>
> For lgamma, the derivative should be digamma / tgamma?
>
> If this is the case, then we still run into a problem with the derivative being too large, since for
> N - n > 1000 or N > 1000, we have binomial_coefficient_log = n * log(N - n) + (N + 0.5) * log(N/(N-n)) + 1/(12*N) - n - 1/(12*(N-n)) - lgamma(n + 1.0).
>
> So when we differentiate the lgamma(n + 1.0), we'd get
> n.d_ * digamma(n + 1.0) / tgamma(n + 1.0), which still results in an error for large n. I'm not too sure what to do about this term.

Ah. I see. I've fixed the problem for binom_coeff_log.

This also means that I need to modify the implementations for lmgamma, but I'm not sure if I interpreted the derivative correctly:

template <typename T1, typename T2>
inline
fvar<typename stan::return_type<T1,T2>::type>

lmgammaa(const fvar<T1>& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2){
using stan::math::lmgamma;
using boost::math::digamma;

using std::log;
double deriv = 0;
int count;
for(count = 1; count < x2.val_ - 1; count++)

deriv += (x1.d_ - x2.d_) * digamma(x1.val_ - (x2.val_ - count) / 2);
deriv += x1.d_ * digamma(x1.val_);

deriv += (2 * x2.val_ - 1) / 2 * log(boost::math::constants::pi<double>()) * x2.d_;
return fvar<typename
stan::return_type<T1,T2>::type>(lmgamma(x1.val_, x2.val_), deriv);
}

Thanks,
Peter

On Feb 4, 2013, at 7:55 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:

> Nope, digamma is the derivative of lgamma (http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/digamma.html).
>
> This means that the derivative of tgamma is actually digamma * tgamma.
>
> On Feb 4, 2013, at 7:03 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>
>> Hi,
>>
>> For lgamma, the derivative should be digamma / tgamma?
>>
>> If this is the case, then we still run into a problem with the derivative being too large, since for
>> N - n > 1000 or N > 1000, we have binomial_coefficient_log = n * log(N - n) + (N + 0.5) * log(N/(N-n)) + 1/(12*N) - n - 1/(12*(N-n)) - lgamma(n + 1.0).
>>
>> So when we differentiate the lgamma(n + 1.0), we'd get
>> n.d_ * digamma(n + 1.0) / tgamma(n + 1.0), which still results in an error for large n. I'm not too sure what to do about this term.

>> But for the derivative as a whole (in terms of x1.d_ and x2.d_) I got

3) I've also run into a problem with Phi (described below).

This is the key error message:

>>       operands to binary expression ('stan::agrad::fvar<double>' and 'int')

You need to define the comparison operators for fvar
and templated alternative types.
What is wrong with using something like this:

template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const fvar<T1>& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2) {
      return x1.val_ < x2.val_;
    }

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const fvar<T1>& x1, const T2& x2) {
      return x1.val_ < x2;
    }

    template <typename T1, typename T2>
    inline bool operator<(const T1& x1, const fvar<T2>& x2) {
      return x1 < x2.val_;
    }
Also, my Phi template in fvar is

template <typename T>
  inline
  fvar<T>
  phi(const fvar<T>& x) {
    using std::exp;
    using std::sqrt;
    using stan::math::Phi;
    return fvar<T>(Phi(x.val_), x.d_ * exp(-x.val_ * x.val_ / 2) / 
      sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()));
  }
and my test code is

TEST(AgradFvar, phi) {
 using stan::agrad::fvar;
 using std::exp;
 using std::sqrt;
 using stan::math::Phi;

 fvar<double> x(0.5);
 x.d_ = 1.0;

 fvar<double> a = Phi(x);
 EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(Phi(0.5), a.val_);
 EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(exp(-0.5 * 0.5 / 2) / 
    sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()), a.d_);

 fvar<double> b = Phi(-x);
 EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(Phi(-0.5), b.val_);
 EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(-exp(-0.5 * 0.5 / 2) / 
    sqrt(2 * boost::math::constants::pi<double>()), b.d_);
}
